title: Lord of the Sea! — Thy Potent Sway
description: Lord of the Sea! — Thy Potent Sway in Tonic Solfa to SELENA, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 828 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Mariner's Hymn”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre, six lines (8.8.8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to SELENA; any other Long Metre, six lines tune fits them as well.
underlay: Lord of the sea! thy po-tent sway Old o-cean's wil-dest waves o-bey; The gale that whis-tles through the shrouds, The storm that drives the fright-ed clouds, If but thy whis-per or-der peace, How soon their rude com-mo-tions cease!

lines: Lord of the sea! — thy potent sway
The gale that whistles through the shrouds,
The storm that drives the frighted clouds, —
If but thy whisper order peace,
How soon their rude commotions cease!
Lord of the sea! — the seaman keep
From all dangers of the deep!
When high the white-capped billows rise,
When tempests roar along the skies,
When foes or shoals awaken fear, —
O, in thy mercy be thou near.
Lord of the sea! — a sea is life
Of care and sorrow, woe and strife!
With watchful pains we steer along,
To keep the right path, shun the wrong:
God grant, that, when we cease to roam,
